newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH HUNTERS MAY KILL 72 WOLVES THIS SEASON.
newsitem.headline: POLISH HUNTERS MAY KILL 72 WOLVES THIS SEASON.

text.p: Polish forestry officials have more than doubled last year's kill limit on wolves due to the exceptional damage they have caused, PAP news agency said on Sunday.

"Between November 1 and the end of February hunters will be allowed to bag a total of 72 wolves in the province of Krosno," PAP news agency quoted Krzysztof Kaminski, spokesman for the Regional Forest Authority, as saying.
He added that the kill limit had been set on the basis of the current wolf population as well as the damage caused by the predators this year.
The 208 wolves living in the heavily-forested southeastern province so far this year have killed 308 stags, 183 roedeer, 80 wild boars and 230 sheep -- a considerable increase over 1995.
Last year, the kill limit for wolves had originally been set at 92, but was slashed to 30 following pressure from ecological groups, the agency said.
Only 20 of the predators were actually shot, PAP added.
Retired French film star and animal-rights activist Brigitte Bardot has been among those campaigning to ban all wolf-hunting in Poland.
